headline: Alan Milburn urges Burnham to spend billions on ‘new deal’ for young people

members.title: How Milburn won over Labour on tackling rising youth unemployment
members.lead: Labour grandee seems to have assuaged MPs’ nerves on need for welfare reform to tackle youth unemployment crisis In a boxing gym in Peterborough almost a year ago, Alan Milburn, freshly appointed to run a government review into the nearly one million young people out of work and education, said he would be “unafraid to shine a light on uncomfortable truths”. The Labour grandee, who had held three cabinet jobs under Tony Blair, warned there was a “downward escalator” taking young people into a “world of benefits” and vowed to provide radical solutions. Many Labour MPs bristled. Continue reading...

members.title: Alan Milburn urges Burnham to spend billions on ‘new deal’ for young people
members.lead: Report on Britain’s youth jobs crisis calls for welfare, education, health and employment policy shake-up Andy Burnham is being urged to spend billions of pounds on a “new deal” for the next generation that would fund guaranteed jobs support for young people to offset a radical cut in benefits. In a watershed report on Britain’s youth jobs crisis, Alan Milburn, the Tony Blair-era health secretary, said the country was at a “fork in the road” after a surge in the number of young people not in education, employment or training (Neet) to almost a million. Continue reading...
